newsitem.title: USA: Three schools qualify for Michigan takeover bill.
newsitem.headline: Three schools qualify for Michigan takeover bill.

text.p: Three Michigan school districts would currently qualify for a state takeover under legislation introduced in the Michigan Senate this week, the sponsor of the measure said Friday.
State Sen. Dan DeGrow, R-Port Huron, said districts in Benton Harbor, Ecorse and Highland Park would be classified as "educationally bankrupt" under the five-bill package he unveiled Thursday.
The bills would create a mechanism for state intervention in school districts that fail to meet minimum standards for educating students.

The legislation, which is supported by Gov. John Engler, gives the governor the power to declare a school district educationally bankrupt and appoint a trustee that would oversee the district, including its finances.
DeGrow said he expects the Senate Education Committee to hold hearings on the legislation in April. He added that the bill faces some opposition among Democrats in the House.
